targetAudience.primary: Architects of agent platforms, plugin hosts and MCP capability boundaries
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands authentication context, plugins and tool invocation.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A requesting capability can forge, widen or reuse authority metadata if the platform treats caller-provided context as evidence.

whyNow: A merged OpenAI Codex maintainer change exposes a concrete local plugin MCP mechanism that strips caller entitlement metadata, verifies current account access in the host and injects a bounded result only across a conjunctively qualified edge.

externalHook.description: The component asking to exercise authority must not also be the issuer of the evidence that grants it.

coreProposition: Authority-bearing access context should be minted by the host that can verify the governing identity, should replace caller-supplied copies, and should cross only an explicitly qualified capability edge; unverifiable state must collapse to a non-authorizing result, while downstream enforcement remains a separate obligation.

originalValue.description: Separates authority issuance, capability eligibility, identity continuity and downstream enforcement into auditable obligations instead of one ambient metadata field.

readerTakeaway: Make the host the authority issuer, strip caller copies, declare every eligibility predicate, bind verification to current identity and define unknown as non-authorizing at both producer and consumer.

supported: Caller-supplied entitlement context is removed before host production.
Verified context is injected only when the documented conjunction of plugin, environment, transport, annotation and argument predicates holds.
Lookup time, redirects, response size and identity continuity are bounded.
Unverifiable or inconsistent state becomes unknown with empty grants.
unsupported: Applicability to all MCP transports or entitlement types
uncertain: How every downstream consumer treats unknown
How revocation is represented when account identity is stable

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article is an independent architecture analysis of a public Codex change.

decisionReason: Inspectable merged implementation and tests support a precise authority-issuance and capability-scope pattern with explicit limits.
